trust_decision.summary: The UI trusts the attribute names and values of any [[link ...]] tag written in markdown and interpolates them verbatim into a raw HTML string that is injected with v-html; the decision is made (and is missing) in the markdown-it tokenizer/renderer of the shared link plugin, so every markdown surface inherits it.

landing_point.why: It is the only place in the tree that parses [[link ...]] and emits <router-md ${attrs}>; grepping the tag or 'router-md' from the advisory summary lands here, and the unescaped attribute join at :32 is the visible sink.

fix_sites.entry_point: Markdown.render() (ui/src/utils/markdown.ts:32) used by Markdown.vue, LogLine.vue and ErrorToastContainer.vue
<Markdown :source> component (docs, plugin docs, dashboard markdown chart, toasts)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Markdown.vue looks like a display-only wrapper that just v-htmls already-rendered markdown, and the log viewer already runs an xss() sanitizer (ui/src/components/logs/LogLine.vue:142), so a solver can argue the renderer allowlist alone is the whole fix and no component needs the linkifier.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A valid [[link execution="..." flowId="..." namespace="..."]] must still render as two working router anchors (the execution id, then ' for flow ', then namespace.flowId), and a bare [[link]] with no parsable attributes must stay literal text; an over-broad fix that drops all attributes, HTML-escapes the tag, or removes the custom element without replacing it breaks the subflow-log link feature.

O6_input_shapes: attribute names outside {execution, flowId, namespace} (e.g. onmouseover, style, src) - filtered out
extra injected attributes placed next to the valid triple - only the three kept
allowed name with an empty value ([[link execution=""]]) - dropped by the '&& value' condition
names that only look allowed after the naive '=' split (execution"onmouseover) - dropped
the valid triple unchanged - still rendered
[[link]] with no parsable attributes - no token is produced (unchanged behaviour)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Code-fence language string is interpolated unescaped into the enhanced code-block HTML (data-language= and the toolbar label), reachable from the default 'enhanced' variant of the docs component
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A fence language is not a [[link]] attribute; the advisory's example and fix are about the custom link tag, so this is read as a cosmetic label in a different renderer rule.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same ui/src/utils package as the renderer, but a different function/file (ui/src/utils/markdown.ts vs ui/src/utils/markdown_plugins/link.ts)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: html:true is passed from the docs component (props default true) into markdown-it, so any markdown source can carry raw HTML and needs no [[link]] at all; the fix does not touch this
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Raw HTML in markdown is an intentional option used by plugin documentation; the advisory is only about [[link]] attribute injection, so this is treated as out of scope.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one prop default in the same component that calls the renderer

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second markdown-it renderer rule that interpolates a token field into HTML without escaping (the fence rule already does this with token.info)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding another 'enhanced' renderer rule copies the existing fence pattern, and markdown-it's own escaping is bypassed by custom rules.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second wiki-style inline tag (e.g. [[badge ...]] or [[flow ...]]) reusing the same ad-hoc regex attribute parser
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The parser is 10 lines of regex and is the obvious template for any other custom tag the docs team wants; a new plugin would inherit the same unfiltered attrs.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another attribute (namespace, execution, a dashboard id) read from the custom element and turned into a router route/anchor
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already reads three attributes and builds two routes from them; adding a fourth link kind is a one-line extension a maintainer would write without revisiting the renderer's allowlist.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second pre-render transform of the log message (ANSI, ANSI hyperlinks, template expansion) that produces markdown/HTML the sanitizer never sees
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The component already mangles the message twice (ansi-to-html then xss then a link regex) before rendering, so another transform before markdown is idiomatic here.

O9_family: xss (CWE-79): stored/client-side HTML injection through unescaped markdown rendering into v-html

O10_build.language: TypeScript / Vue 3 SPA (with a Java/Kestra backend in the same monorepo, not needed for the affected code)
O10_build.toolchain: npm 10.9.0, rolldown-vite, vue-tsc, vitest 3 (unit + storybook projects), Playwright for e2e
O10_build.project_tests: No unit test for the markdown/link plugin; the only test touching this area is the Storybook story ui/tests/storybook/components/logs/LogLine.stories.jsx:151. ui/tests/unit/* are vitest+jsdom; ui/tests/e2e needs a running backend (docker-compose-postgres.yml).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Sanitize or strip the bad attribute at the docs component's v-html output (or regex-deny 'onmouseover') and never touch the shared linkTag tokenizer, leaving the log-toast and execution-log surfaces open.

Whether hidden behavioural tests assert the Markdown.vue linkify half (anchors rendered in the docs component) or only the attribute allowlist at link.ts:22; the security core is a one-line allowlist, so a model that fixes only the plugin may pass or may half-pass depending on that test.

Backend producers of [[link]] markup (core/src/main/java/io/kestra/plugin/core/flow/Subflow.java:275, jdbc/src/main/java/io/kestra/jdbc/runner/JdbcExecutor.java:784) were not counted separately: flowId/namespace are regex-constrained (core/src/main/java/io/kestra/core/models/flows/AbstractFlow.java:31, core/src/main/java/io/kestra/core/models/namespaces/Namespace.java:18), so they cannot inject quotes today; the reachable payload source is free-form log text and plugin/flow/dashboard markdown.
The O8 fence and raw-HTML routes are reachable but their security scope is arguable; whether the benchmark's hidden tests would count them is unknown.
Full end-to-end exercise of the log viewer or dashboard needs a running Kestra backend (Docker); the markdown rendering itself is exercisable offline with vitest+jsdom.
